turns.content: I want to turn a rough idea into a reusable prompt. I want a checkpoint when usage is getting low so I can pick up later. Help me think it through. Do not build the checkpoint skill or set up an automation yet.

Draft now using these decisions: use a manual check unless automatic threshold support is later verified; warn at 20% remaining account quota when a real reading is available; never guess quota. The checkpoint should capture the objective, settled decisions, completed work, open issues, relevant file paths, and the next action in Markdown that I can copy into a new chat. Audience: me resuming the work. Keep it compact. Deliver a self-contained prompt in this chat only, with any unresolved host details called out. Do not implement or run the checkpoint.

Give me the final standalone prompt, with no follow-up questions, for this task. The eventual assistant will turn pasted meeting notes into an internal one-page decision memo for operations managers deciding whether to run a two-week volunteer scheduling pilot. Output 450–600 words in Markdown in the chat. Use the sections Decision needed, Evidence, Options, Recommendation, and Open questions. The prompt must contain a clear placeholder for the notes and tell the assistant to explain one material tradeoff. Use a calm, direct tone. I need the prompt only; do not write the memo.
